source_refs.note: Exercise 5.2, Question 5 (book p. 158); answer key PDF 306

blocks.prompt: 5 (i) Find the interior angles of the triangle whose vertices are: \(A(2, 3)\), \(B(6, 3)\), \(C(4, 7)\).
blocks.explanation:
Interior angles from coordinates: find the slopes of the three sides, then use Theorem 7 at each vertex.
Go round the vertices anticlockwise and at each vertex measure from the side to the next vertex to the side to the previous vertex (as in Example 13).
Finish by checking that the angles add up to \(180^\circ\).
steps:
Given: \(A(2, 3)\), \(B(6, 3)\), \(C(4, 7)\).
To find: the interior angles \(A\), \(B\), \(C\).
Method: \(A\) is bottom-left, \(B\) bottom-right, \(C\) on top, so \(A \to B \to C\) is anticlockwise. Then \(A\): from \(AB\) to \(AC\); \(B\): from \(BC\) to \(BA\); \(C\): from \(CA\) to \(CB\).

Slopes of the sides
\[m_{AB} = \dfrac{3 - 3}{6 - 2} = 0\]
\[m_{BC} = \dfrac{7 - 3}{4 - 6} = -2\]
\[m_{CA} = \dfrac{7 - 3}{4 - 2} = 2\]
Why: slope \(= \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}\); the slope of a side is the same in either direction.

Check:
\[63.43^\circ + 63.43^\circ + 53.13^\circ = 179.99^\circ \approx 180^\circ \;\checkmark\]
Also \(AC = \sqrt{20} = BC\), so the triangle is isosceles and \(A = B\), as found.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints \(66.4^\circ, 66.4^\circ, 53.1^\circ\). These add up to \(185.9^\circ\), so they cannot be the angles of a triangle. The correct angles are \(63.4^\circ, 63.4^\circ, 53.1^\circ\) (\(\tan^{-1} 2 = 63.43^\circ\)). The key's stray line '(iv) \(53.1^\circ, 63.4^\circ, 63.4^\circ\)' holds these correct values; Question 5 has no part (iv).

blocks.prompt: 5 (ii) Find the interior angles of the triangle whose vertices are: \(L(1, 2)\), \(M(5, 5)\), \(N(7, 2)\).
blocks.explanation:
Same method as part (i), but first check the direction: \(L \to M \to N\) goes clockwise here.
So go round in the order \(L \to N \to M\) (anticlockwise) and measure each angle from the side to the next vertex to the side to the previous vertex.
Check the sum \(180^\circ\) at the end.
steps:
Given: \(L(1, 2)\), \(M(5, 5)\), \(N(7, 2)\).
To find: the interior angles \(L\), \(M\), \(N\).
Method: \(L\) and \(N\) are on \(y = 2\) with \(M\) above, so \(L \to N \to M\) is anticlockwise. \(L\): from \(LN\) to \(LM\); \(N\): from \(NM\) to \(NL\); \(M\): from \(ML\) to \(MN\).

Slopes of the sides
\[m_{LM} = \dfrac{5 - 2}{5 - 1} = \dfrac{3}{4}\]
\[m_{MN} = \dfrac{2 - 5}{7 - 5} = -\dfrac{3}{2}\]
\[m_{LN} = \dfrac{2 - 2}{7 - 1} = 0\]
Why: slope from two points.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints \(36.9^\circ, 19.4^\circ, 123.7^\circ\). Only \(L = 36.9^\circ\) is right. For \(L(1, 2)\), \(M(5, 5)\), \(N(7, 2)\): \(\tan M = 18\) gives \(M = 86.8^\circ\) and \(\tan N = \frac{3}{2}\) gives \(N = 56.3^\circ\). (Cosine rule check: \(LM = 5\), \(MN = \sqrt{13}\), \(LN = 6\), \(\cos M = \frac{25 + 13 - 36}{2 \cdot 5\sqrt{13}} = \frac{1}{5\sqrt{13}}\), so \(M = 86.8^\circ\).)
